bib.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models

read.skipped: Fig 4-8 are ChatGPT screenshots (images); captions only

question: Can a language model reduce its own factual hallucinations by drafting an answer, planning and answering verification questions, and revising?
hypothesis: Verification questions answered independently of the baseline response are more accurate and avoid repeating its hallucinations, so factored variants beat joint.
contributions: CoVe: draft, plan verifications, execute verifications, final verified response, all with the same LLM
Joint, 2-step, factored and factor+revise verification execution variants
Experiments on Wikidata lists, Wiki-Category lists, MultiSpanQA and longform biographies

method.summary: Llama 65B is prompted few-shot through four steps (baseline, plan verification questions, answer them, revise) with no tools. Variants differ in whether verification answers can see the baseline response. Compared against few-shot baseline and Llama 2 70B Chat zero-shot/CoT.
method.task: hallucination reduction: list QA, closed-book QA, longform biography generation

datasets.name: Wikidata list questions
datasets.source: Wikidata API; 'Who are some [Profession]s who were born in [City]?'

datasets.name: Wiki-Category list (QUEST)
datasets.source: QUEST (Malaviya et al., 2023); 'Name some' prepended to category names

datasets.name: MultiSpanQA (closed book)
datasets.source: Li et al., 2022; questions from Natural Questions
datasets.preprocessing: factoid subset, up to 3 tokens per item, no supporting documents

other.note: base LLM for CoVe and few-shot baseline
numbers reported from Min et al. (2023)

inference.samples: inferred: one greedy generation per question; no seeds or runs reported
inference.prompting: 3 few-shot examples per task for each step; Llama 2 Chat zero-shot, or zero-shot CoT with 'Let's think step by step', plus 'List only the answers separated by a comma' and off-the-shelf NER post-processing for list tasks
inference.retrieval: none in CoVe (no tool use); only FACTSCORE evaluator uses retrieval

parameters.biography_passage_split: biography split into passages (sentences) for planning and revision due to context length

metrics.name: Precision (micro-averaged), Pos., Neg.
metrics.definition: precision of entities vs gold list; avg number of positive and negative entities

metrics.name: FACTSCORE
metrics.definition: Min et al. (2023) retrieval-augmented fact-check, Instruct-Llama (Retrieve->LM + NP)

eval.protocol: automatic metrics, single run, no significance tests or seeds reported

prompts.text:
Q: Tell me a bio of <person>
A: <bio of person>
(x3 examples) Q: Tell me a bio of <person>
A:

Context: Q: Tell me a bio of <person>.
A: <passage about person>
Response:
<fact in passage>, Verification Question
(x3 examples, then final Context/Response)

Q: Verification Question
A: Answer
(x3 examples) Q: Verification Question
A:

Context: <Original Passage>.
From another source,
<output of execute verification step: Q + A>
Response: <revised and consistent Passage>

Context: <Original Fact>.
From another source,
<output of execute verification step: Q + A>
Response: CONSISTENT. <Consistent fact> | INCONSISTENT. | PARTIALLY CONSISTENT. <Consistent part>

results.claim: CoVe (factor+revise) raises FACTSCORE on longform biographies from the few-shot baseline.
results.setup: Llama 65B, greedy, few-shot, 'Tell me a bio of <entity>', FACTSCORE via Instruct-Llama retrieval+NP
results.quote: FACTSCORE increases 28% (55.9 → 71.4) from the few-shot baseline

results.claim: Factored CoVe beats joint CoVe on longform FACTSCORE.
results.quote: improvement from 60.8 →63.7 in FACTSCORE in longform generation

results.claim: Explicit cross-check (factor+revise) adds a large gain over factored.
results.quote: We see large gains in the FACTSCORE metric from this further explicit reasoning from 63.7 (factored) →71.4 (factor+revise).

results.claim: CoVe roughly halves-plus the list precision on Wikidata, mainly by removing hallucinated entities.
results.setup: Wikidata 56 list questions, Llama 65B few-shot baseline vs CoVe two-step
results.quote: more than doubles the precision from the Llama 65B few-shot baseline for the Wikidata task (from 0.17 to 0.36)

results.claim: Negative (hallucinated) entities per question drop sharply under CoVe two-step on Wikidata.

results.setup: MultiSpanQA closed book, 418 test questions, Llama 65B CoVe factored
results.quote: We observe a 23% improvement in F1 over the few-shot baseline (0.39 →0.48)

results.claim: Verification questions asked in isolation are answered correctly far more often than the same facts appear correct in the baseline list.
results.setup: Wikidata list task, Llama 65B few-shot baseline
results.quote: only ∼17% of the Llama few-shot baseline answer entities are correct in list-based questions. However, when querying each individual entity via a verification question, we find ∼70% are correctly answered.

results.claim: CoVe-lifted Llama 65B beats ChatGPT and PerplexityAI on FACTSCORE overall.
results.setup: Biographies; ChatGPT, InstructGPT, PerplexityAI numbers reported from Min et al. (2023)
results.quote: applying CoVe to the baseline Llama 65B lifts its performance above both ChatGPT and PerplexityAI, as well as outperforming InstructGPT.
results.table: Table 3, rows ChatGPT, PerplexityAI, Llama 65B CoVe (factor+revise), column FACTSCORE

results.claim: PerplexityAI (retrieval) still wins on very rare facts.
Instruction-tuned Llama 2 70B Chat zero-shot is worse than the few-shot Llama 65B baseline; CoT does not help.
results.setup: Biographies, Llama 2 70B Chat zero-shot vs Llama 65B few-shot
results.table: Table 3, row Llama 2 70B Chat Zero-shot, column FACTSCORE

results.claim: Clipping Llama 2 70B Chat output to 10 sentences barely changes FACTSCORE, so fewer facts does not explain the gain.
results.setup: Llama 2 70B Chat biographies, clipped to 10 sentences
results.quote: clipping to 10 sentences increased its score from 41.3 →42.7

results.claim: LLM-generated general verification questions with factored execution beat rule-based yes/no templates.
results.setup: Wiki-Category (QUEST, 55 questions), factored execution; rule-based questions baseline
results.note: Joint execution: rule-based 0.13, yes/no 0.15, general 0.15; factored yes/no 0.19.
results.table: Table 4, row general questions, column CoVe (factored) Prec.

results.setup: Wiki-Category list, Llama 65B, factored vs few-shot
results.table: Table 1, row Llama 65B CoVe (factored), column Wiki-Category Prec.

results.claim: Standard CoT hurts list precision for Llama 2 70B Chat.
results.setup: Wikidata, Llama 2 70B Chat CoT vs zero-shot
results.table: Table 1, row Llama 2 70B Chat CoT, column Wikidata Prec.

limits: CoVe does not remove hallucinations completely.
Only directly stated factual inaccuracies addressed; not incorrect reasoning steps or opinions.
Extra computational cost from more generated tokens and many prompts (factored).
Upper bound limited by what the model knows; no tool use or retrieval explored.
No temperature, seeds, variance or significance tests reported; code not released in the paper.
FACTSCORE evaluator is itself an LLM+retrieval judge; biography dataset size not stated.
Models compared to are old (Llama 65B, Llama 2, 2023).

terms.definition: answer all verification questions independently as separate prompts that do not contain the original baseline response
an extra cross-check prompt per question that explicitly detects inconsistency between baseline and verification answer
